s1.syndrome_frame: Acute neurological syndrome with fever, quadriplegia, and brainstem involvement
salient_findings: Bilateral horizontal gaze palsy with impaired oculocephalic reflexes
Quadriplegia with bilateral extensor plantar responses
T1 hypointensity and T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the bilateral thalami, pons, medulla, and left cerebellum on MRI
key_facts: 18-year-old woman
2 days of fever and vomiting
1 day of weakness in all four limbs and speech difficulty
Temperature was 101.4 °F
Normal vital signs except for fever
Fully conscious (GCS 15)
Normal fundoscopic examination
Bulbar dysarthria
No signs of meningeal irritation
Anemia, reduced packed cell volume, and thrombocytopenia on laboratory evaluation
Normal total cell count with all lymphocytes on cerebrospinal fluid analysis
Mildly elevated protein on cerebrospinal fluid analysis
Serum dengue NS1 antigen was positive
MRI showed T1 hypointensity and T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the bilateral thalami, pons, medulla, and left cerebellum

shortlist.label: Dengue encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Serum dengue NS1 antigen was positive and patient has fever, vomiting, and neurological symptoms

shortlist.label: Japanese encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has fever, vomiting, and neurological symptoms, and Japanese encephalitis is a common cause of acute neurological syndrome in endemic areas

shortlist.label: Acute disseminated encephalomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has neurological symptoms and MRI findings consistent with demyelination

shortlist.label: Bickerstaff's brainstem encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has brainstem involvement and neurological symptoms consistent with Bickerstaff's brainstem encephalitis

shortlist.label: West Nile virus infection
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has fever, neurological symptoms, and West Nile virus infection is a possible cause of acute neurological syndrome

raw.rationale: The presence of serum dengue NS1 antigen and the clinical presentation of fever, vomiting, and neurological symptoms such as bulbar dysarthria and quadriplegia, along with the characteristic MRI findings, support the diagnosis of dengue encephalitis.

rejected.label: Japanese encephalitis
rejected.why: No specific mention of exposure to mosquitoes that transmit Japanese encephalitis or relevant travel history

rejected.label: Acute disseminated encephalomyelitis
rejected.why: Lack of typical post-infectious or post-vaccination context and absence of characteristic periventricular white matter lesions on MRI

rejected.label: Bickerstaff's brainstem encephalitis
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and MRI findings do not specifically point towards brainstem encephalitis without additional features like ophthalmoplegia

rejected.label: West Nile virus infection
rejected.why: No mention of specific exposure to mosquitoes that transmit West Nile virus or relevant clinical and laboratory findings
